text:
maya: Heads-up — since the preempt-window rollout in ap-southeast1 last night we're seeing a spike in tiny evictions and a weird fragmentation pattern. Pods with fractional GPU requests are getting bounced between nodes every 30s. :face_with_raised_eyebrow:
jon: ugh. any graphs?
rick: /sig events show a lot of `Preempting` then `Binding` churn. pasted a sample k8s event: ```Normal Preempt 30s kube-scheduler Preempting pod gpu-job-92 for higher priority job```
tina: is this the same as the tiny-pod pingpong we've seen before or new?
maya: superficially similar but different timing — it's aligned with the preempt-window (we open one 60s slot per rack). looks like the scheduler is re-evaluating fractional placements during the window and kicking low-priority tiny pods repeatedly. :eyes:
jon: could be the scheduler's tie-breaker logic + fractional requests. do we have the allocation snapshot?
rick: grabbed a heap of allocation snapshots from the rack. key pattern: node A has 0.125 gpu free, node B 0.1, scheduler tries to gang-pack and preempts the 0.05 slack on A to fit a 0.25 request => causes eviction cascade.
tina: maybe we should bias the preempt-window to avoid fractional reshuffles. or add a soft-affinity to keep tiny pods anchored for 2m.
autoscaler-bot: [alert] ap-southeast1 autoscaler scaled down gpu-pool-ps to 2 nodes -> 1 node at 2026-03-21T02:14:27Z (policy: aggressive-scale-down).
maya: autoscaler downscale plus preempt-window is the perfect storm. downscale removes warm-slot holes, scheduler tries to compact and ends up shifting tiny pods.
jon: proposed short-term mitigations: 1) pause preempt-window for that rack 2) increase grace period on tiny pods (`terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 120`) 3) add `scheduler.alpha.kubernetes.io/affinity: preferAvoid` for fractional pods.
rick: I can push a hotfix to the scheduler tie-breaker (prefer no-preempt if fractional slack < 0.2) — but needs a canary.
tina: for immediate relief can we add a taint on the nodes during scale-down e.g., `node.kubernetes.io/preempting=true:NoSchedule` and let running tiny pods finish?
maya: good idea. do we have signal that kubelet honours that quickly?
jon: kubelet will respect nodeAffinity/taints on scheduling decisions; existing pods won't be evicted by that alone but new scheduling will avoid them. so combined with a short pause on preempt-window it should stop the churn.
rick: I'll coordinate a canary patch + taint rollout. plan: 1) pause preempt-window for ap-southeast1 rack-3 2) taint nodes in that pool 3) patch scheduler tie-breaker on canary subset 4) monitor evictions for 20m.
tina: will update SLO dashboard and add an annotation to the ongoing incident.
maya: thanks team. quick ask — capture one sample evicted pod's logs+profile and drop in the incident thread. helps us confirm no mispredicted resource accounting. :thumbsup:
jon: on it, will paste shortly.
rick: pasted pod/ gpu-job-92 evict log link: https://internal.logs/redwood/ap-southeast1/gpu-job-92/evict.log :link:
maya: seeing it. looks like the eviction was due to `Preemption` for `batch-critical` job. moving to mitigation now.
autoscaler-bot: [info] manual scale action: scaled gpu-pool-ps to 2 nodes at 2026-03-21T02:16:10Z (by rick).
jon: after 10m of the taint+pause we should see evictions drop. will report back.
tina: adding note: consider a longer-term change to the allocator to respect fractional slack thresholds and bias against preempting fractional pods during scale-down windows.
maya: filed follow-up ticket INFRA-1147 with proposed changes and measurements. allocating owners: rick + jon.
jon: thanks — I'll own the allocator PR and can pair with rick on the canary.
maya: closing the loop here once we have 20m of stable metrics. :wave:
